name: Alexisonfire
label: Distort Entertainment
lede: Five kids from St. Catharines named themselves after a porn star's website, sold platinum in Canada with three singers screaming over each other, broke up badly, and came back to win a Juno thirteen years after their last album.

eras.title: Three bands die, one is born
eras.text: In St. Catharines, Ontario, three local bands fell apart at the same moment and their survivors pooled into one. Alexisonfire had three vocalists, a clean singer, a screamer and a guitarist who did both, and a word-of-mouth following that outran their distribution deal.

years.h: Alexisonfire forms from the wreckage of three St. Catharines bands
years.p: George Pettit (Condemning Salem), [[Dallas Green|06b65c62-b894-45ec-88f4-b7d689851e35]] (Helicon Blue), Wade MacNeil and Chris Steele (Plan 9) and drummer Jesse Ingelevics start a band after their old groups break up at the same time.
years.xp: They billed themselves as the sound of two Catholic high-school girls in mid-knife-fight. The line-up split vocals three ways: Green sang clean, Pettit screamed, MacNeil did both.

years.h: Alexis Fire, the adult actress, threatens to sue over the name
years.p: Alexisonfire took its name from adult performer Alexis Fire's website. According to Wikipedia she threatened legal action, but the name wasn't registered and nothing came of it.

years.h: The Math Sheets Demo, named for Jesse Ingelevics' homework
years.p: Alexisonfire's first demo came wrapped in drummer Jesse Ingelevics' math homework. Engineer Greg Below and journalist Mitch Joel heard it while starting a label, Distort Entertainment, and signed the band.

years.h: Alexisonfire comes out on Halloween · Distort
years.p: Alexisonfire's self-titled debut, released through Distort with EMI distribution in Canada. Wikipedia credits its success mostly to word of mouth; it went gold in Canada in October 2005.

years.h: Alexisonfire crosses Canada twice and plays Hellfest
years.p: Alexisonfire tour Canada twice with [[Billy Talent|fd429857-5ace-4609-ae54-1502c3bdac11]] and Spitalfield, play Hellfest, and tour Europe with [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]], after earlier Ontario and New York runs with [[Gwar|f7ccd53a-234c-4800-8d1b-21b201bad1de]] and [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]].

eras.title: Gold in twelve weeks
eras.text: Watch Out!, made in producer Julius Butty's home studio near Hamilton, took Alexisonfire from a word-of-mouth band to a chart act. Equal Vision brought it to the US. Then the drummer left and Dallas Green started a quiet solo project that would change everything.

years.h: Watch Out! debuts at No. 6 in Canada
years.p: Alexisonfire's second album sold 6,580 copies in its first Canadian week, went gold in twelve weeks and platinum by 2007. Equal Vision released it in the US three weeks later.

years.h: "Pulmonary Archery" wins Best Video at the Canadian Independent Music Awards
years.p: Alexisonfire's "Pulmonary Archery" clip wins Best Video, and the band are named Favourite Indie Band at the CASBY Awards.

years.h: Alexisonfire win New Group of the Year at the Junos
years.p: Alexisonfire take the 2005 Juno for New Group of the Year, and the "Accidents" video wins Best Independent Video at the MuchMusic Video Awards.

years.h: Jesse Ingelevics leaves; Jordan Hastings takes the drums
years.p: Drummer Jesse Ingelevics quits Alexisonfire. Jordan Hastings, formerly of Jersey, replaces him, and the band spends the rest of 2005 on the road, including Reading and Leeds and Japan's Summer Sonic.

years.h: Dallas Green launches [[City and Colour|b1003bf1-25b8-41f4-a783-36060f987913]]
years.p: Dallas Green starts City and Colour, a quiet solo folk project. It becomes a hit in its own right and, six years later, one of the reasons Alexisonfire breaks up.

eras.title: Number one, and a boat on the Thames
eras.text: Crisis made Alexisonfire one of the biggest bands in Canada and a festival draw in the UK and Australia. The follow-up came out on a new label run by their old manager. Underneath the touring, the band was coming apart.

years.cap: Crisis, 2006: the cover draws on the Great Lakes blizzard of 1977
years.h: Crisis enters the Canadian chart at No. 1
years.p: Alexisonfire's third album sells over 20,000 copies in its first Canadian week and goes platinum by May 2007. The launch party is on a boat on the River Thames in London.
years.xp:
Recorded at Metalworks in Mississauga and Silo Recording in Ontario in early 2006 with Julius Butty. Gared O'Donnell of [[Planes Mistaken for Stars|ff428f12-1c80-4437-bfff-0e9af6ff94c9]] appears on "You Burn First", and the title track draws on the Great Lakes blizzard of 1977. In the US it came out on Vagrant Records, not Equal Vision.

A ten-month world tour followed: Reading and Leeds, Festival d'été de Québec, a headline at Brixton Academy. Kerrang! later ranked Crisis 50th among the 50 greatest albums of the 21st century.

years.h: "This Could Be Anywhere in the World" wins at the MuchMusic Video Awards
years.p: Alexisonfire's video wins Best Cinematography; the band are nominated for Group of the Year at the Junos. The single goes gold in Canada in 2018.

years.h: Wade MacNeil admits Alexisonfire are at a crossroads
years.p: Wade MacNeil says Alexisonfire hasn't broken up but is at a crossroads. Breakup rumors run through the next year while Dallas Green sketches heavier, weirder songs later released as the Dog's Blood EP.
years.xp: George Pettit once said the band wanted to kill screamo rather than save it, a line Wikipedia notes he later regretted. The four-song Dog's Blood EP, sketched in 2008, came out in 2010.

years.h: Alexisonfire sign to Dine Alone, their ex-manager's label
years.p: Alexisonfire join Dine Alone Records, founded by former manager Joel Carriere. They had started recording Old Crows / Young Cardinals on February 1.

years.h: Old Crows / Young Cardinals · Dine Alone
years.p: Alexisonfire's fourth album, with "Young Cardinals" as the single. It starts a tour of roughly 300 dates that runs to December 2010.

years.h: A barrier collapses at Alexisonfire's Winter Olympics show
years.p: Seconds into a free all-ages Alexisonfire show at Live City Yaletown during the Vancouver Olympics, the crowd barrier gives way. About 20 people are slightly injured.

years.h: The hometown show nobody knew was the last
years.p: Alexisonfire close the Old Crows / Young Cardinals tour in their hometown. Dallas Green later treated it as the band's final concert.

eras.title: Not amicable
eras.text: Dallas Green's City and Colour had grown too big to share his time, and Wade MacNeil got an offer to front a British punk band. The breakup was ugly enough that the farewell had to wait a year.

years.h: Alexisonfire promise a fifth album heavier than Dog's Blood
years.p: Alexisonfire tweet that they're writing a new record so heavy it will make Dog's Blood sound like ska. Six months later the band is over.

q: Being in Alexisonfire was killing me.
years.h: Alexisonfire break up after Dallas Green and Wade MacNeil leave
years.p: George Pettit announces the end, citing Green and MacNeil's exits and personal issues among the rest. Green had left to focus on [[City and Colour|b1003bf1-25b8-41f4-a783-36060f987913]]; MacNeil to front the UK band [[Gallows|4cb159df-bd09-4f42-bfec-09b6a248a52f]].
years.xp: Green said the strain of running both bands had led to a nervous breakdown. Pettit described the split as not amicable. A tenth-anniversary Canadian tour and a series of releases that had been planned were dropped.

years.h: Dallas Green and Wade MacNeil talk about one last run
years.p: Dallas Green says he and MacNeil want a proper goodbye, because at Alexisonfire's real last show nobody knew it was the last.

years.h: Death Letter EP reworks songs from all four Alexisonfire albums
years.p: Alexisonfire release Death Letter, new versions of songs from each of their four records, as the farewell tour begins. The tour grows from nine dates to 30 across Canada, the UK, Australia and Brazil.

years.h: Alexisonfire's farewell at Copps Coliseum, Hamilton
years.p: Alexisonfire play what's billed as their last show at Copps Coliseum in Hamilton, Ontario. The recording comes out in 2016 as Live at Copps on four records and Blu-ray.

eras.title: Officially back
eras.text: The farewell lasted two years. Alexisonfire returned as a part-time band with one singer now a professional firefighter, and when the new album finally came it won them a Juno.

years.h: Alexisonfire's 1,000-copy vinyl box sells out in 30 minutes
years.p: A Christmas Day box set of all four Alexisonfire albums plus EPs and B-sides sells out in half an hour. A slightly smaller second edition follows in August 2014.

years.h: Alexisonfire announce reunion shows, Reading and Leeds included
years.p: Alexisonfire book Reading and Leeds, Heavy Montréal, Riot Fest and more, their first shows since the farewell.

years.h: Wade MacNeil tells Riot Fest Toronto Alexisonfire is officially back
years.p: On stage at Riot Fest in Toronto, MacNeil announces the band is back for good. The band later clarifies it has no immediate plans for new music.

years.h: "Familiar Drugs": first new Alexisonfire song in nearly nine years
years.p: Fans found the numbers 2, 15 and 19 hidden in three black images on Alexisonfire's Instagram by pushing the brightness. The date was the release of "Familiar Drugs".

years.h: George Pettit reveals he's been a firefighter since 2015
years.p: George Pettit tells the Toronto Star he became a professional firefighter in 2015, and that the job comes first even with Alexisonfire back.

years.h: Otherness, Alexisonfire's first album in thirteen years
years.p: Announced March 10 and released on Dine Alone. Otherness wins Rock Album of the Year at the 2023 Junos.

years.h: Alexisonfire cover [[The Tragically Hip|e86ab653-bec8-46f3-b4b6-a1a866919ef6]] on Copies of Old Masters, Vol. 1
years.p: Alexisonfire's covers EP on Dine Alone arrives with their version of the Hip's "Fully Completely".

years.h: Alexisonfire finish a new album and debut "Dogs of Chernobyl"
years.p: After recording from February, Alexisonfire announce the album is done at a Crisis 20th-anniversary show at RBC Amphitheatre and debut "Dogs of Chernobyl".
